hints: Focus on what type of functional group can be oxidised all the way to a carboxylic acid under reflux with acidified dichromate(VI).
Both propan-1-ol and propanal can give propanoic acid on strong oxidation, so use the sodium test to decide between an alcohol and a carbonyl compound.
Remember alcohols fizz with sodium to give hydrogen gas, while aldehydes and ketones do not, so pick the oxidisable compound that is not an alcohol.
walkthrough:
**Use the oxidation result**

Heating under reflux with acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is strong oxidation. Only two types give a carboxylic acid.

$$\text{primary alcohol} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{aldehyde} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{carboxylic acid}$$

**Shortlist the candidates**

Propan-1-ol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) is primary, so it oxidises to propanoic acid. Propanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$) is an aldehyde, so it oxidises to propanoic acid too.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + [O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$

**Use the sodium test**

Alcohols contain $\text{-OH}$ and react with sodium metal to release hydrogen. Aldehydes and ketones have no $\text{-OH}$ and do not react.

$$2\text{R-OH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{R-ONa} + \text{H}_2$$

**Conclude the identity**

Compound X makes an acid but does NOT react with sodium, so it cannot be an alcohol. It must be the aldehyde, propanal.

options.A: Propanal is an aldehyde. It is easily oxidised by refluxing acidified dichromate(VI) to propanoic acid, and it has no -OH group so it does not react with sodium metal. It fits both observations perfectly.
options.B: Propanone is a ketone. Ketones resist oxidation by acidified dichromate(VI) and do not give a carboxylic acid. Students sometimes forget that only primary alcohols and aldehydes go to acids.
options.C: Propan-1-ol is a primary alcohol so it would give propanoic acid on reflux, but it would also react vigorously with sodium to give hydrogen gas. It fails the second test.
options.D: Propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol. It oxidises only to a ketone (propanone), not to a carboxylic acid, and it would also react with sodium. It fails both tests.
